title: Make K-Subarray Sums Equal
statement:
The integer array `arr` is circular: the element after the last one is the first one again. One operation adds 1 to, or subtracts 1 from, a single element of your choice.

Consider the `arr.length` windows of `k` consecutive elements, one starting at every index (a window may run past the end and continue from the start). Return the minimum number of operations after which all of these windows have the same sum.
notes:
## Intuition

Two neighbouring windows share all but one element: the window starting at `i + 1` drops `arr[i]` and gains `arr[(i + k) % n]`. Their sums are equal exactly when those two elements are equal, so the goal is `arr[i] === arr[(i + k) % n]` for every `i`. Jumping by `k` around a circle of `n` positions visits exactly the indices that agree modulo `g = gcd(n, k)`, so the array splits into `g` independent groups, and every group must end with one common value. Moving a set of numbers to a common value costs least when that value is their median.

## Approach

1. Compute `step = gcd(n, k)` with Euclid's algorithm.
2. For each `start` from 0 to `step - 1`, collect the group `arr[start], arr[start + step], ...`.
3. Sort the group and take its middle element as `median`.
4. Add `|value - median|` for every value in the group to `total`.
5. Return `total`.

## Example 1, step by step

`arr = [1, 4, 1, 3]`, `k = 2`, so `n = 4` and `step = gcd(4, 2) = 2`.
- `start = 0`: group `[1, 1]`, median `1`, cost `0`.
- `start = 1`: group `[4, 3]` sorts to `[3, 4]`, median `4`, cost `1`.

The answer is `0 + 1 = 1`.

## Complexity

- Time: O(n log n): every element lands in one group, and sorting the groups costs at most a full sort.
- Space: O(n) for the group being sorted.

## Pitfalls

- Groups come from `gcd(n, k)`, not from `k` alone; because the array wraps, `i` and `i + k` keep linking until the cycle closes.
- The mean is not the right target; the sum of absolute differences is smallest at the median.
- The answer can reach about `10^14`, so Java and C need a 64-bit total.

## Variables

| Name | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `step`, `rest`, `remainder` | Euclid's algorithm; `step` ends as `gcd(n, k)` |
| `start` | first index of the current group |
| `group` | values at `start, start + step, ...` |
| `median` | middle value of the sorted group, the target for all of it |
| `total` | operations counted so far |

narration.5: Keep going until the remainder reaches zero.

narration.12: There is one independent group for each residue modulo the gcd.
narration.14: Indices that differ by a multiple of the gcd must hold equal values.
narration.17: Sort the group so its median sits in the middle.
narration.18: The median minimises the total distance the group's values must move.
narration.19: Each value moves to the median one unit at a time.
narration.20: Those unit moves are the operations this value needs.
narration.23: The sum over all groups is the minimum number of operations.
